facts.raw_span: born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
weighing 2152 g
one of monochorionic diamniotic twins
her identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound had shown microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI of the head revealed microcephaly, marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles without signs of elevated intracranial pressure
severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum were preserved
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions were seen
very weak light reflexes bilaterally
mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign
No chorioretinal dysplasia was noted

concepts.why: The presence of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes supports this diagnosis.
The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and thinning of the brain lobes is consistent with this condition.
The presence of weak light reflexes and mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign supports this diagnosis.
The finding of marked enlargement of the lateral ventricles and thinning of the brain lobes is consistent with this condition.
The presence of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and abnormal brain morphology supports this diagnosis.
The low birth weight and history of twin death in utero support this diagnosis.
The history of monochorionic diamniotic twins and the death of one twin in utero supports this diagnosis.
The presence of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and abnormal brain morphology supports this diagnosis.
The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and thinning of the brain lobes is consistent with this condition.
The premature birth and low birth weight support this diagnosis.
It explains the selective preservation of certain brain structures and absence of intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions.
It explains the optic nerve pallor and suspected peripapillary double-ring sign in the context of cerebral anomalies.

rationales.F01: Premature birth may be related to various complications.
rationales.F04: Intrauterine death of a twin can cause complications in the surviving twin.
rationales.F05: Microcephaly and ventricular enlargement are indicative of brain abnormalities.
rationales.F06: Postnatal MRI findings confirm prenatal ultrasound results.
rationales.F07: Severe thinning of brain lobes suggests significant brain damage.
rationales.F10: Weak light reflexes may indicate optic nerve issues.
rationales.F11: Optic nerve pallor and peripapillary double-ring sign are specific findings for optic nerve hypoplasia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes with preservation of the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum points towards a prenatal brain disruption sequence, which is further supported by the absence of intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions.
